messages:
maria-cs: Hey team, customer reports a sudden wave of 429s starting at 2024-11-02T15:02:00Z. They say it spikes right after token refreshes for their fleet of mobile clients. Can we triage?

lina: :eyes: which endpoints are returning 429s? auth or generation?

maria-cs: Mainly /v1/chat and streaming create endpoints. They included server logs + a curl sample from their proxy.

samir: Paste the curl and a log snippet please. Also which SDK version are they on?

maria-cs: SDK v1.4.2 (mobile). Snippet:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'```

maria-cs: and their server log extract:```2024-11-02T15:01:59Z token.refresh user_id=acme-123 issued_at=1698945679
2024-11-02T15:02:00Z request start req_id=abcd1234 path=/v1/chat client=mobile-app instance=12
2024-11-02T15:02:00Z request start req_id=abcd1235 path=/v1/chat client=mobile-app instance=13
2024-11-02T15:02:01Z response 429 req_id=abcd1234 reason=rate_limit
2024-11-02T15:02:01Z response 429 req_id=abcd1235 reason=rate_limit```

ada: This looks like a token refresh stampede: many clients refresh at the same time and then immediately flood requests. Do we see any upstream rate-limit headers in those 429 responses?

maria-cs: They forwarded the raw response headers: `x-rw-rate-limit: 120/60; x-rw-rate-remaining: 0; x-rw-retry-after: 1` (from the edge).

ryan: :thumbsup: confirms rate window exhaustion. Two quick asks: 1) confirm whether the requests share the same token or different tokens issued at same time, 2) capture client refresh timestamps distribution.

maria-cs: The mobile clients each get their own token from the customer's auth service but they all renew at the same server-side cron boundary. Tokens issued within the same second.

samir: Ok plausible. Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) Ask customer to add jitter to token refresh (randomize +-30s), 2) Cache tokens at a per-device process layer so not every thread hits auth at once, 3) Implement leaky-bucket smoothing on their side. Also we can offer a short-term quota bump for their org.

ada: From infra side, we should verify our edge buckets: are those requests being folded into a single tenant window or split? If their tokens are identical across devices then edge treats them as same tenant. Check our auth->edge logs for token fingerprinting.

ops-bot: [ratecap-metrics] tenant=acme-123 window=60s capacity=120 used=121 spike=+180 at 2024-11-02T15:02:00Z

ryan: That matches. Also check client TLS session reuse and HTTP/2 multiplexing — clients may open many concurrent streams after refresh. If multiple concurrent streams per connection, we might see a burst that exhausts per-tenant concurrency.

maria-cs: Customer is willing to apply client-side fixes; they asked what exact repro steps/dev logs we need.

samir: Ask them to gather: 1) token refresh timestamps (epoch seconds) for a 5-minute window around the spike, 2) per-instance request rates, 3) SDK config (concurrency limits, keepalive), 4) one full raw 429 response (headers+body) and the edge timestamp.

lina: I'll own the contact and ask for a sanitized packet capture + their cron/refresh code snippet. Also I'll offer a temporary org-level rate bump for 30m while they test.

ada: Short-term server-side mitigations we can offer: enable token-based smoothing at the edge (heuristic: detect many tokens issued at same epoch -> apply implicit jitter or soft-queue), or add a short per-token warmup limit. Both need ops approval.

ryan: Ops approval: I think a short, controlled soft-queue is low-risk. If we deploy, we need to monitor latency SLO and backpressure.

lina: Customer asked for exact code to add jitter. Suggestion for mobile clients:```// pseudo
let refreshInterval = tokenTTL - 60 // base
let jitter = Math.floor(Math.random() * 30) - 15 // +-15s
setTimeout(refreshToken, refreshInterval + jitter)```

maria-cs: Customer will try that + reduce parallel streams from 8->2 and report back. They're happy to accept a 30m quota bump.

samir: I've filed a short ticket to infra to check token-fingerprint grouping and add observability for 'tokens_issued_per_second' metric. Ticket #OPS-9851.

ada: Follow-up steps for this thread: 1) Lina to confirm quota bump & collect customer artifacts; 2) Samir to validate edge token folding logs; 3) Ops to evaluate soft-queue.

lina: I'll update when quota bump is active. Leaving a note: if customer still hits 429s after jitter, escalate to dedicated call and we can capture pcap.

maria-cs: Thanks all :pray: will loop in customer and send the artifacts within the hour.

samir: Marking resolved for now unless new 429s after the mitigation test. :white_check_mark:
